test_title: PYST 8: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 01 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which Indian River has received the most national attention for severe ecological damage caused by illegal sand mining, particularly in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ganga** river, spanning approximately **2,525 km**, is the most significant river in India, but it has faced severe ecological degradation due to **illegal sand mining**, particularly in the states of **Uttar Pradesh** and **Bihar**.
 
• Illegal extraction of sand from the riverbed of the **Ganga** has led to the depletion of **groundwater** levels, alteration of the river's natural course, and massive **soil erosion** along the banks.
 
• The **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** has frequently intervened, issuing several bans and strict guidelines to regulate mining activities in **Uttar Pradesh** and **Bihar** to prevent further damage to the **Ganga** ecosystem.
 
• This activity poses a direct threat to endangered species such as the **Gangetic Dolphin** (India's national aquatic animal) and the **Gharial**, as their nesting and breeding grounds are destroyed by heavy machinery used in mining.
 
• The **Namami Gange Programme**, an Integrated Conservation Mission launched in **June 2014**, recognizes the control of illegal mining as a vital component for the **rejuvenation** and **pollution abatement** of the river.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Krishna River**:

 
 
• It originates at **Mahabaleshwar** in **Maharashtra** and flows through **Karnataka**, **Telangana**, and **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• While it also faces sand mining issues, it is more frequently in the news for **inter-state water sharing disputes** between the riparian states.
 
 
 
• **Palar River**:
 
 
• This is an **ephemeral river** flowing through **Karnataka**, **Andhra Pradesh**, and **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It has suffered extreme ecological damage and **groundwater depletion** due to rampant sand mining in the **Vellore** and **Kanchipuram** districts of **Tamil Nadu**, though it receives less "national" attention compared to the **Ganga**.
 
 
 
• **Narmada River**:
 
 
• Known as the "**Life Line of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat**," it is the largest west-flowing river in India, flowing through a **rift valley**.
 
• Sand mining occurs in the **Narmada** basin, but the river is globally recognized more for the **Narmada Bachao Andolan** and the construction of the **Sardar Sarovar Dam**.
 
 
 
• **Legal Status of Sand**:
 
 
• In India, sand is classified as a "**minor mineral**" under the **Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957**.
 
• The **State Governments** have the power to frame rules for the grant of quarry leases and the regulation of mining for minor minerals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ecological Impact**: Excessive sand mining causes the riverbed to deepen (**incising**), which can lead to the collapse of **bridge foundations** and other infrastructure.
 
• **Sustainable Sand Mining Management Guidelines (2016)**: These were released by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to promote scientific mining and monitoring through **Remote Sensing** and **GIS**.
 
• **Data Fact**: India is the second-largest consumer of **sand** in the world after **China**, driven largely by the booming **construction** and **infrastructure** sectors.
